## ✨ Highlights

- 🧩 **Janus without the Controller, from your own orchestrator**: a private cloud with its own orchestration can drive nodes directly, in any language. The new docs specify every contract a node offers - the fleet's certificates and bundle, first contact, the gRPC API with each call's role - and an [example](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/own-orchestrator.md#the-example) in shell drives three real nodes on every image build, with no Controller and no janusctl.
- 🔒 **The Controller's updater runs Docker Compose v5.6.0**, which fixes two containerd vulnerabilities (medium).

## 📚 Documentation

- **[Your own orchestrator](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/own-orchestrator.md)**: what the Controller does and what replaces it, the life of a node, and how stable the `v1alpha1` API is.
- **[Certificates and the fleet](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/orchestrator-certificates.md)**: the bundle's exact format, the client certificate profile, roles, calls made for a user, and what an enterprise PKI has to do - made with `openssl` alone in the example.
- **[First contact](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/first-contact.md)**: a node you create, trusted from its serial console; or a node announcing itself to a registration endpoint you serve - the protocol, specified.
- **[Driving nodes](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/driving-nodes.md)**: code for your language from the `.proto` files, `grpcurl`, the errors, and the safe way to apply a configuration, try a network change and update a node.
- **[Node API reference](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/api-reference.md)**: every call, the role and the domain it needs, what it does - generated from the `.proto` files and the roles nodes enforce.

## 🔌 The node API

- No call or field changed. Every call now has its own comment in the `.proto` files - code generated in any language carries it - and `ApplyConfiguration`, `MetaWrite` and `MetaDelete` say they answer `Unimplemented`.
- From this release on, these notes say when the API changes.

## 🖥️ Nodes

- **The node's CA on its console, in one line a program reads**: every boot prints `pki: this node's CA: SHA-256 <hex>` - what an orchestrator pins a new node's CA with ([first contact](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/first-contact.md#its-ca-from-its-console)). The banner still shows it for people.
- **Let's Encrypt**: go-jose 4.1.5 in the letsencrypt extension's ACME client - its fixes for malformed input and key checks.

## 🔒 Security

- **Docker Compose v5.5.1 → v5.6.0**, in the Controller's updater (`janus-controller-updater`) - the containerd code it carries:
  - 🟡 medium [CVE-2026-53493](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6597) - an image pull made to exhaust resources with a crafted OCI index;
  - 🟡 medium [CVE-2026-53495](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6444) - a goroutine leak in CRI's ExecSync.

  The updater pulls the Controller's own image from Docker Hub, and doesn't use CRI: the exposure was small. Updating the Controller is enough - nodes aren't concerned.

## 📦 Dependencies

- The Controller's frontend: lucide-react 1.51.0, vite 8.3.2 - nothing changes on its pages.
- Left for later: Alpine 3.24 (the static HAProxy built against its musl crashes), grpc 1.84.0 (it brings a vulnerability into janusd), Go 1.27 (the toolchain moves for the whole tree at once).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Update the Controller** (from its page, or `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`): its updater carries the fixes above.
- **Nodes**: optional - for the console line an orchestrator reads, and the letsencrypt extension's go-jose.
